summary: The Santee Sioux Nation is a Dakota nation whose people call themselves Isanti. Its members descend largely from the Mdewakanton and Wahpekute bands, part of the Santee division of the Dakota, who lived in the woodlands and lake country of present-day Minnesota, farming and living in villages for much of the year. Through a series of treaties the Dakota gave up most of their Minnesota land. Promised payments and supplies often failed to arrive, and hunger and distrust grew until war broke out in Minnesota in 1862. Afterward the Army imprisoned many Dakota people, and a military commission tried the accused without lawyers. The federal government then carried out a mass execution at Mankato and shipped Santee families by boat to Crow Creek in Dakota Territory, where many died of disease and hunger. In 1866 a presidential order set aside land along the Missouri River in northeastern Nebraska for the Santee at Crow Creek, and the people moved there. Allotment later cut the reservation sharply. Today the reservation lies in Knox County, Nebraska, with the Missouri River on its northern edge. The Santee campus of Nebraska Indian Community College teaches Dakota language and culture.

notes: The Santee Sioux Nation's website (santeesiouxnation.net) blocked automated reading this pass; the tribally chartered Nebraska Indian Community College was used as the primary tribal-side source. The number executed at Mankato (38) and deaths at Crow Creek (more than 300) are single-source (NICC) and left out; reviewers may restore them from a second source. Reservation acreage figures and the Santee Normal Training School dates are left out as single-source. Reviewers should confirm whether 'Isanti' or 'Isanyathi' and 'Dakota Oyate' are the nation's preferred self-names, and where the tribal government seat should be named (Santee village vs. Niobrara).
